newsitem.title: UK: Graseby says Q1 sales rose 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: Graseby says Q1 sales rose 16 pct.

text.p: British electronic instruments group Graseby Plc said on Thursday that its group sales rose 16 percent in the first quarter of 1997 over the same period a year ago.
The group chairman John Jackson told an annual meeting of shareholders that the growth came largely from the medical business.
"International market conditions remain competitive as a result of the strength of sterling. However, Graseby continues to grow and is performing in line with our expectations," Jackson said.
The company's medical sales were almost double the 1996 level, which reflected 15 percent organic growth in the original business.
Product monitoring sales were 10 percent higher than in the first quarter of 1996 and included a strong performance in North America.
The company had announced on May 19 that the U.S. Defense Department ACADA contract to Graseby had been increased by $21 million to $77 million.
"This brings the value of total overseas defence contracts to more than 70 million stg," Jackson said.

Jackson also said that John Hawkins of Philips Electronics NV will succeed Paul Lester as the company's chief executive. Lester will be leaving the company on June 30 to join engineering firm Balfour Beatty Ltd.
